name: Manasseh
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Hezekiah was one of the very few righteous kings, so righteous that the Most High extended his life, and Manasseh his son reigned in his stead.
Kings gives more detail on the northern kingdom and Chronicles on the southern, so the class reads both accounts of Manasseh.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Hezekiah sleeps with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigns in his stead.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: Manasseh king of Judah seduced them to do more evil than did the nations whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel. He did wickedly above all that the Amorites did, and made Judah also to sin with his idols. The Amorites were terrible; Manasseh went above them.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: The Lord said Israel would not be moved out of the land, only if they would observe to do according to all that Moses commanded. But they hearkened not: and Manasseh seduced them to do more evil than did the nations whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel. We went crazier than the heathen.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: The Most High speaks by His servants the prophets that because Manasseh did wickedly above all the Amorites and made Judah to sin, He is bringing such evil upon Jerusalem that both ears of whoever hears it shall tingle.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: Manasseh sheds innocent blood very much, filling Jerusalem from one end to the other, beside the sin with which he made Judah to sin.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: His remaining acts are written in the chronicles of the kings of Judah, and the prayer of Manasseh is recorded in the Apocrypha, prayed while he was held captive in Babylon.
Chronicles shows the captains of the king of Assyria took Manasseh among the thorns and carried him with fetters to Babylon, then a province under Assyria; there he repented and prayed.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: The history shows a power struggle beginning, where Assyrian kings ruled over Babylon, and later Babylonian kings ruled over Assyria; Manasseh sleeps with his fathers and Amon his son reigns.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: He beat down the altars on the roof of Ahaz's chamber and the altars Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, and cast their dust into the brook Kidron.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

points: This came upon Judah at the commandment of the Lord to remove them out of his sight for the sins of Manasseh and the innocent blood he shed, which the Lord would not pardon.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: The record runs through Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, and Josiah, keeping the royal succession by name.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: All Judah honoured Hezekiah at his death and buried him in the chiefest of the sepulchres of the sons of David, and Manasseh reigned in his stead.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: When the ambassadors of Babylon come to inquire of the wonder, God leaves him to try him and know his heart. Hezekiah then sleeps with his fathers, is buried in honour among the sons of David, and Manasseh his son reigns in his stead.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: Manasseh made Judah err and do worse than the heathen the Lord had destroyed before them, the nations Joshua and the elders were sent to kill out of the land for the very same works.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: The Lord spoke to Manasseh and the people through the prophets, but they would not hearken, because they assumed the son of so righteous a father must be righteous too.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Wherefore the Lord brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, which took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: So the Lord brought the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, who took Manasseh among the thorns, the wicked leaders under him, bound him with fetters and carried him to Babylon.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: The Most High speaks to Manasseh and his people, but they will not hearken, so he brings upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria.
They take Manasseh among the thorns, bind him with chains, and carry him to Babylon. The kings of Israel that were once kings are brought down into captivity, exactly as the curses warned.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

points: And when he was in affliction, he besought the Lord his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers, and prayed unto him. That is where the Prayer of Manasses in the Apocrypha comes from. And God was intreated of him, heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the Lord he was God.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Locked up in Babylon he humbled himself greatly, the Lord heard his supplication and brought him back to his kingdom, and then Manasseh knew that the Lord he was God.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: The Most High is entreated of him, hears his supplication, and brings him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom, and then Manasseh knows that the Lord he was God. This is the pattern of 2 Chronicles 7:14, that a people called by his name who humble themselves will be heard.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

points: The rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, are written in the book of the kings of Israel, and his prayer and how the Most High was entreated of him are written among the sayings of the seers.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

points: This is the prayer of Manasseh, a writing of the Apocrypha found before the Maccabees, which is part of the Bible. Manasseh sleeps with his fathers and Amon his son reigns in his stead.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

points: Amon reigned two years and did evil as his father had done, sacrificed to the carved images Manasseh had made, and humbled not himself as Manasseh had humbled himself, but trespassed more and more. Hezekiah was righteous, Manasseh wicked and then humbled, and Amon followed the bad example.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Amon is twenty two years old when he begins to reign and reigns two years in Jerusalem, doing evil in the sight of the Lord as Manasseh his father, sacrificing to all the carved images Manasseh had made.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

cases.name: Manasseh
cases.charge: Building again the high places his father destroyed; altars to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the Lord’s house; his children through the fire; observing times, enchantments, witchcraft, familiar spirits and wizards; a carved image in the house of God; Jerusalem filled with innocent blood from one end to another
cases.preview: Manasseh began to reign at twelve and reigned fifty-five years, undoing his father Hezekiah’s reform and leading Judah to do worse than the heathen the Lord had cast out: altars to the host of heaven…
